source.snippet: I'd gladly pay $17 a year — hell ten times that — to not see ads on Instagram. However, the fact that I can and would pay for that means that Meta can't afford to lose me, because it kills the value of their audience.

problem_statement: Professionals and high-income users would willingly pay a meaningful subscription fee to use major social platforms without advertising, but platforms have no incentive to offer this, leaving a persistent unmet preference for ad-free social consumption.
target_segment: High-income professionals and knowledge workers who use Instagram, Facebook, or similar ad-supported platforms daily and have expressed explicit willingness to pay for an ad-free experience.
notes: Commenter explicitly states willingness to pay $170/year. The structural barrier is that Meta cannot offer this without cannibalizing ad revenue — not a product gap a solo operator can directly fill. However, adjacent opportunities exist: browser-based ad-blocking subscription services, curated ad-free content newsletters, or social feed management tools that reduce ad exposure. Signal strength kept low because no direct product opportunity is available — this is a preference signal, not an actionable gap for a solo builder.
